text:
maia: FYI: found intermittent malformed JSON during streaming tool calls from onyx-ptq-canary. happens with long context + kvcache enabled.

maia: raw chunk A:
```json
{"op":"create_ticket","args":{"title":"svc OOM","tags":["infra",
``
maia: raw chunk B:
```json
"pagerduty"],"details":"OOM on shard 3"}}
```

oliver: looks like a mid-array split leaving an extra comma at the end of chunk A. our stitcher currently strips leading/trailing commas and waits for close. that might be unsafe for PTQ splits.

shreya: can we try a two-pass approach: 1) a non-destructive lenient repair (json5-ish) that flags changes, 2) if repair mutates structure significantly, trigger a full regen. also record raw token boundaries in telemetry.

vik: agreed. ensure repaired outputs are marked so downstream callers know they were heuristically fixed. and add a rate cap for regen to avoid thundering canaries.

maia: local patch healed ~65% of cases but observed array merging in ~3% — unacceptable for billing/alerts routes. we'll restrict auto-accept to non-critical endpoints.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled back onyx-ptq-canary to onyx-ptq-stable at 5923456798 due to parse spike.

maia: next steps: shreya will enable high-sample raw-stream capture for onyx-ptq-canary (include quant_opset, kvcache flag, stream chunk sizes). i'll run combinatorial runs (kvcache on/off x stream true/false x quant variants) and post matrix results tomorrow.

oliver: ping infra-team: might need to add a streaming-stitcher integration test using PTQ-generated chunked outputs to catch this early.

shreya: noted. adding test vectors and sampler now.
